lesson.title: Ratios: Comparing Two Amounts

steps.say: Hi friend, it's Ms. Yuanyuan! Look at my fruit bowl this morning. I have four apples and six oranges. If someone asks me, how many oranges compared to apples, I don't want to say a long story. I want a quick way to compare two amounts. That quick way is called a ratio.

visual.caption: Four apples and six oranges in the bowl

steps.say: Here is how we write it. Apples to oranges is four to six. We write it with a little two dot mark, like four two dots six. This kind of ratio compares one part to another part, so we call it a part to part ratio. The order matters! Four to six means apples first, oranges second.

Now let's compare a part to the whole bowl. Four apples plus six oranges makes ten pieces of fruit altogether. So apples to all the fruit is four to ten. That's a part to whole ratio, and a part to whole ratio can also be written as a fraction: four tenths, which is the same as two fifths.

Here's the magic part. Ratios can be dressed up in different sizes and still mean the same thing. If I shrink four to six by dividing both numbers by two, I get two to three. If I grow it by multiplying both numbers by one and a half... let's keep it simple, multiply two to three by three and you get six to nine. Two to three, four to six, six to nine — all the same mix! Those are called equivalent ratios. The rule is: whatever you do to one number, do the very same thing to the other.

visual.caption: A ratio table: each column is the same mix

steps.say: Let's try one together. You're packing trail mix for a hike up the Grouse Grind. In one scoop there are eight almonds and twelve raisins. Almonds to raisins is eight to twelve. Can we make it simpler? Both eight and twelve can be divided by four. Eight divided by four is two, and twelve divided by four is three. So eight to twelve is the same as two to three. Nice and tidy!

visual.caption: 8 almonds to 12 raisins, which simplifies to 2 to 3

steps.say: Now the part to whole for that same trail mix. Eight almonds plus twelve raisins is twenty pieces in total. Almonds to total is eight to twenty, which is two fifths. Raisins to total is twelve to twenty, which is three fifths. Look at the two bars: two fifths almonds, three fifths raisins, and together they fill up one whole scoop.

visual.caption: Almonds two fifths, raisins three fifths

steps.say: One more, a little bigger. Your blueberry smoothie recipe uses two scoops of blueberries for every three cups of milk. Today you're making a giant batch with eight scoops of blueberries. How much milk? Two grows to eight by multiplying by four, so the milk must also be multiplied by four. Three times four is twelve. You need twelve cups of milk. Two to three is the same mix as eight to twelve!

visual.caption: Multiply both rows by the same number

steps.say: So that's a ratio: a friendly way of comparing two amounts. Part to part compares one group to another group, part to whole compares one group to everything, and equivalent ratios are the same mix wearing different sized numbers. Great work today!

lesson.answer: A ratio compares two amounts — and as long as you multiply or divide both numbers by the same thing, the ratio stays the same.

practice.question: At a Granville Island market stall, a bag holds 6 red apples and 9 green apples. Write the ratio of red apples to green apples in its simplest form, and write the part-to-whole ratio of red apples to all the apples in the bag.
practice.answer: Red to green is 6 : 9, and dividing both by 3 gives 2 : 3. Altogether there are 6 + 9 = 15 apples, so red to total is 6 : 15, which simplifies to 2 : 5 (that is, two fifths of the apples are red).
